comparison: Perfect agreement on severe autoimmune phenotype (C4, C35-C44, C78). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing across survival, histopathology, and immune parameters. OpenEval notes 'severe and well-documented' phenotype; peer reviewers state 'strong phenotype supports critical role.'

Perfect agreement on in vitro vs in vivo functional discrepancy (C5, C47-C51). Both accept that CXXC1 KO Tregs maintain in vitro suppression but fail in vivo models. OpenEval describes 'context-dependent defects'; peer reviewers explicitly note this is 'partly due to diminished survival.'

Perfect agreement on negative findings (C66-C68). Both evaluations accept that DNA methylation and H3K4me1 are unchanged, establishing specificity for H3K4me3. OpenEval emphasizes importance for 'establishing specificity'; peer reviewers note this strengthens mechanistic conclusions.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic distinction (C73-C75). Both accept that FOXP3 binding is maintained while H3K4me3 is affected, showing CXXC1 functions as cofactor. OpenEval notes this is 'important for understanding how CXXC1 functions'; peer reviewers implicitly accept this interpretation without concerns.

Agreement on proposed Set1/COMPASS mechanism (C80, C82), though both acknowledge speculative elements. OpenEval notes 'direct demonstration in Treg cells is not shown'; peer reviewers accept mechanism as consistent with known CXXC1 function without challenge.

Divergent evaluation of therapeutic potential claim (C9). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of therapeutic validation studies and need for additional evidence. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting translational implications based on significance of findings.

Perfect agreement on background/contextual claims (C1, C10-C18, C79, C81, C83-C84). Both evaluations accept these as established literature providing necessary context. OpenEval notes 'appropriately cited'; peer reviewers did not challenge any contextual claims.

Strong agreement on FOXP3 binding at H3K4me3-enriched promoters (C20, C22-C29). OpenEval includes C19 (validation control); peer reviewers address C19 separately in R15. Both accept converging evidence from multiple genomic approaches.

Strong agreement on reduced H3K4me3 at broad domains (C3, C69-C70, C72, C76-C77). Peer review R10 also includes C71 not in OpenEval R3. Both identify this as key mechanistic finding with all reviewers noting novelty and importance.

Strong agreement on scRNA-seq findings (C52-C55, C57-C58). OpenEval includes C59 (proliferation markers); peer review includes C56 (functional markers). Both accept comprehensive single-cell analysis showing altered Treg phenotypes.

Partial agreement on genomic co-occupancy (C30-C33). OpenEval R2 also addresses protein interaction (C2, C34) which peer reviewers evaluate separately in R3. Both accept CUT&Tag evidence for genomic overlap as convincing.

Partial agreement on CXXC1-FOXP3 interaction (C2, C34). OpenEval R2 groups interaction data with genomic binding; peer reviewers evaluate protein interaction separately. Both accept co-IP and immunofluorescence evidence.

Overlap on genomic co-localization (C7-C8). OpenEval R11 addresses this as separate finding; peer review R2 includes these claims with broader genomic binding analysis (C30-C33). Both accept the co-occupancy evidence.

Partial agreement on transcriptional profiling (C63-C65). OpenEval R8 also includes C60-C62 (het-KO experimental design); peer reviewers focus on gene expression changes. Both accept RNA-seq evidence for altered Treg signature genes.

Partial overlap on het-KO findings (C60-C62). OpenEval R8 emphasizes het-KO design controlling for inflammation; peer review R6 groups these with other dysfunction markers (C6, C45-C46, C59). Both accept cell-intrinsic defects.

Partial overlap on increased Treg numbers (C45-C46). OpenEval R12 evaluates this as separate paradoxical finding; peer review R6 groups with broader dysfunction phenotype (C6, C59-C62). Both accept the observation.

Partial overlap on functional marker expression (C6, C56, C62, C65). OpenEval R6 groups multiple markers together; peer review R6 includes these with homeostasis defects (C45-C46, C59-C61). Both accept reduced expression across markers.

Minimal overlap on C65 (marker expression). OpenEval R6 groups C65 with other functional markers; peer review R8 includes C65 with transcriptional profiling. Both accept the finding through flow cytometry and RNA-seq.

Minimal overlap on C19 (validation control). OpenEval R1 includes C19 with main FOXP3 binding findings; peer reviewers evaluate C19 separately as quality control for CUT&Tag methodology. Both accept without concerns.
Minimal overlap on C56 (functional markers). OpenEval R6 groups C56 with other markers; peer review R7 includes C56 with scRNA-seq analysis. Both accept reduced expression evidence.
Minimal overlap on C59 (proliferation/activation). OpenEval R7 includes C59 with scRNA-seq findings; peer review R6 groups C59 with dysfunction phenotype. Both accept the observation.
